title: fallthrough: Describe a Number
hints: Swift cases don't fall through unless you write `fallthrough`.
Start with `"The number \(n) is"`; the prime case appends its text and falls through; `default` appends `" an integer."`.
`case 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19: description += " a prime number, and also"; fallthrough`.
jsBridge: JS `switch` falls through **by default**, a famous source of bugs. Swift does the reverse: no implicit fall-through, and an explicit `fallthrough` keyword when you really want it (rarely).

compass.q: How many JS bugs come from a forgotten `break`? Why is Swift's opt-in `fallthrough` the better default?
Can `fallthrough` jump into a case that binds variables with `let`? Why not?
`fallthrough` vs extracting the shared code into a function: which would a reviewer prefer?
Have you ever seen `fallthrough` in production Swift? What's a legitimate use?
